cor:interface-never-realises-isospin-wei:
Corollary No admissible interface element realises either isospin weight: the two mechanisms compute on disjoint sets. Under the hypotheses of the band separation, every admissible interface scalar \mu = z + d with d \in [-h,\,0] satisfies

  \mu \;\ne\; \mu_-
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \mu \;\ne\; \mu_+ .

Strict inequalities on both sides give the two non-equalities directly. Stated this way the result is the sharpest form of the obstruction: it is not that the interface reproduces an isospin weight badly, it is that the interface never reproduces one at all.

Two mechanisms, disjoint ranges

The isospin mechanism selects the bound channel and the interface mechanism produces the binding number, and it has never been shown that they are the same object. The corollary settles that they are not. The values the interface can take form the interval [z-h,\, z]; the values isospin assigns are the two points \mu_- and \mu_+; and the interval separates the points without containing either. Using the T = 0 projector as the interface element is therefore not an unmotivated choice; it is an unavailable one.

What a repair would have to change

The obstruction was first posed as a dimension count: the bond family \mathrm{span}\{1, \sigma_2\} reaches only a 2-plane of the four-dimensional V_{(2,1)} block. The present statement is the same obstruction read on the observable side, where it becomes quantitative --- the two targets miss the reachable interval by 63.22\,\% and 22.85\,\%.

That reading also says what will not work. Tuning d moves a point inside an interval that does not contain the target; choosing a crossing sign selects an endpoint of the same interval; choosing a different q moves both endpoints and both targets together, and the margins are wide enough that no admissible q closes them. A repair must change the arena. Two candidates remain open: enlarging H_3(q) to H_4(q), which widens the reachable set from 2 to 5 parameters inside a nine-dimensional block, or pairing the isospin label to the bond in some way other than identifying the projector with the interface. Neither is carried out here, and the first carries its own risk --- three extra parameters that are not themselves derived would convert a clean impossibility into a fit with room to hide.
rem:colour-tube-floor-overshoots-deutero:
Remark The colour-tube selection rule cannot supply the interface tilt: a category error, corroborated by a family floor above the deuteron. The colour-tube channel weight is a natural candidate for the interface tilt d: it already assigns a rational weight to each pair of colour sheets, it is normalised, and it is upstream of the same D_6 structure the interface sits in. It cannot supply the tilt, and the reason is a category error rather than a numerical miss.

The category error

The colour-tube weight is a function W_{c_1c_2}(F_1, F_2) of two colour sheets and two nucleon colour contents, where a content is a definite assignment of a quark flavour to each of the three sheets --- (u,u,d) for the proton, (u,d,d) for the neutron. The chirality sign it is built from compares F_1 at sheet c_1 against F_2 at sheet c_2, so the whole construction presupposes that each nucleon of the pair has a definite flavour content.

The deuteron does not. Its flavour state is the antisymmetric line (pn - np)/\sqrt2, on which F_1 and F_2 are not definite: the state is a superposition of the two content assignments, and the weight is not a linear functional on the flavour space but a function of the labels. Evaluating W_{c_1c_2} on the deuteron therefore requires a choice of branch that the construction does not supply, and any such choice breaks the exchange antisymmetry that defines the channel. The obstruction is structural: it is a property of what the weight is allowed to depend on, exactly as in the content-keyed refutation, and no adjustment of the weights repairs it.

The numerical corroboration, and what backs it

Independently of the above, the family the rule generates has been scanned for the pn binding it would predict. The figures in this paragraph are provisional: they are recorded from an exploratory scan and are not yet reproduced by a committed producer, so no witness backs them. Scanning the mixing parameter on a hundredth grid across the six colour alignments at thirty digits gives a family floor of B_{pn} = 2.29580\ \mathrm{MeV}, against the measured B_{\mathrm{AME}}({}^2\mathrm{H}) = 2.224566\ \mathrm{MeV} --- an overshoot of 0.0712\ \mathrm{MeV}, or 3.2\,\%, by the most favourable member of the family. The S_3 average that confinement demands lands higher still, at 2.46755\ \mathrm{MeV}, some 11\,\% above target. Reaching the measured value requires a mixing parameter of 0.35768, which is to say it requires knowing the answer first.

The two arguments are of different kinds and should not be conflated. The category error excludes the construction outright; the scan reports that this family, on its own and on the grid scanned, does not reach the target. The scan is corroboration, and it is the weaker of the two.

Convergence with the band separation

Three independent routes now arrive at the same wall. The interface band lies strictly between the two isospin weights, so no admissible element realises either; the colour-tube family's floor sits above the deuteron; and the content-keyed proposal is refuted by the two pn channels. Each closes a different way of trying to derive the tilt from structure already in hand, and none of them is closed by a better parameter. What they leave standing is the arena question: whether widening the algebra, rather than re-weighting inside it, is where the tilt comes from.

sec:nuclear-binding-intro: Once the two-nucleon isospin channel is selected, extending the linear-programming deficit profile across the (Z, N) lattice determines the global stability landscape of composite nuclei. This section defines the LP demand profile and demand stability criterion, proves that the nuclear binding operator partitions the (Z, N) chart into three distinct structural regimes—the torus-knot regime for light nuclei, the Hopf-link regime across intermediate shells, and the post-magic regime above closed shells—and formulates the periodic-table demand conjecture linking deficit minima to the empirical magic numbers.
def:demand-profile:
Definition Demand profile of a derived atom. Let \mathcal{A}(Z, N) = \sum_w c_w \cdot w be a derived atom in normal form. Its demand profile is

  \mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A})
  \;=\;
  \{(w, c_w) : c_w < 0\}
  \;\subset\;
  \mathrm{NF}(B_A) \times \mathbb{R}_{<0}.

The demand magnitude is |\mathrm{dem}| = \sum_{c_w < 0} |c_w|.
prop:demand-stability:
Proposition Demand profile determines nuclear and atomic stability. The derived atom \mathcal{A}(Z, N) is:

  1. Beta-stable if and only if, for all single nucleon exchanges \mathfrak{p} \leftrightarrow \mathfrak{n} at fixed A = Z + N:
  |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z, N))|
  \;\leq\;
  |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z \pm 1, N \mp 1))|.

The stable configuration minimizes the demand magnitude at fixed A.

  1. Shell-closed if and only if \mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}) = \varnothing. All NF coefficients are non-negative.
  2. Doubly magic if both the nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) and the atom \mathcal{A}(Z, N) have locally minimal Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M among neighboring (Z, N).

The demand-free {}^3\mathrm{He} and the Markov-trace-minimal {}^4\mathrm{He} represent two distinct stability mechanisms: shell closure (zero demand) and action minimization (lowest trace).

Connection to beta decay

The e^- demand channel in the nucleon normal form represents beta decay balance. A nucleon with c_{e^-} < 0 is topologically configured to emit an electron. The transition \mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} + e^- + \bar\nu occurs when:

  |c_{e^-}(\mathfrak{n})| > |c_{e^-}(\mathfrak{p})|
  \quad \text{and} \quad
  \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n}) < \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{p}).

At q_0, both conditions hold. Thus, the free neutron beta-decays.

Inductive scaling via transfer matrix identities

For nuclei with A > 4, the NF computation scales polynomially via inductive Gröbner--Shirshov reduction. The key identity is the transfer matrix factorization: the product of two inter-nucleon crossings reduces via the Hecke relation before the next nucleon is appended. For same-type nucleon pairs:

  C_{pp} \cdot C_{pp} = h_{\mathrm{A}} \cdot C_{pp} + \mathbf{1},
  \qquad
  C_{nn} \cdot C_{nn} = \mathbf{1} - h_{\mathrm{A}} \cdot C_{nn}.

These are instances of the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}} \sigma_i + \mathbf{1} applied to typed crossings. They ensure that iterated same-type nucleon pairs do not increase the NF complexity beyond linear growth in the number of nucleons.

Witness scope and multi-precision grid (all-nuclides-sdp-admissibility-mp)

A multiprecision recomputation at 50 dps (+10 guard digits), with decimal-string transport into the linear-program solver, supersedes the legacy float64 sweep:

  • Multi-precision synthetic magic-Z-dense (Z, N) grid (4,932 rows): evaluates Z \in [0, 92], with full N \in [0, 160] scans (161 / 161 rows solved) at every magic proton shell Z \in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82\} and 47 neutron-number points per non-magic Z (including 93 / 93 rows solved at every magic neutron shell N \in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}), achieving nf_overflow_count = 0 and rows_carrying_mpfr_dual = 4,932.

prop:nuclear-operator-regimes:
Proposition Three operator regimes for nuclear binding. In the inductive construction of \mathcal{N}(Z, N), the inter-nucleon binding operator \Phi_k selected at step k for the nuclei recorded in this chapter belongs to one of three regimes:

(Regime I — Shell filling.) At the first step of the first nuclear shell, the selected operator is the five-crossing three-strand braid

  \Phi_k = (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2\sigma_0
  \qquad (k = 1,\; p \to pp),

whose closure is the T(2,4) torus link.

(Regime II — Magic shell closure.) At and immediately after a magic number, the selected operator is L_\pm (closure in B_3: the unknot):

  \Phi_k \in \{L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1,\; L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0\}

The L_\pm operators, whose closures are the unknot, achieve demand closure at magic shell boundaries.

(Regime III — Open shell.) Beyond a closed magic shell, the selected operator reverts to the bare typed crossing:

  \Phi_k \in \{C_{pp},\; C_{pn},\; C_{nn}\}

The operator transitions from (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2\sigma_0 to L_+ at the first magic number, then to L_- at the shell boundary, and finally to C_{pn} in the open shell. The \mathcal{B}_3 Borromean operator is not selected at any recorded nuclear step; it appears only as the quark-level confinement operator.
rem:nuclear-operator-regimes-interpretat:
Remark Physical interpretation of the three nuclear binding regimes. The three operator regimes carry this physical interpretation:

  • Regime I (torus knot): Initial nucleons interact as individual particles. The residual strong force between them forms the cinquefoil T_{2,5}.
  • Regime II (Hopf link): At magic numbers, the filled shell acts collectively. A new nucleon crosses the entire shell rather than individual nucleons. This collective Hopf link binds the new nucleon, driving shell closure.
  • Regime III (bare crossing): Beyond the magic shell, the nucleus is large enough that new nucleons interact via simple pairwise crossings. The existing normal form already encodes the collective effects.
rem:nuclear-regimes-shadow-price-kinks-p:
Remark Prior art for toric chamber flips, magic-shell shadow-price kinks, and finite-nucleon phase walls. The regime transitions in Three operator regimes for nuclear binding and the integer cluster assembly in Physical cluster chamber, drip-line monomer reduction, and the Hoyle triple-alpha bottleneck realize a sharp geometric mechanism that connects combinatorial optimization, density-functional theory, and nuclear shell physics.

Two-layer Gröbner architecture: microscopic \mathrm{HeckeGS} versus macroscopic \mathrm{ChamberGS}

Nuclear assembly separates into two distinct reduction layers:

  1. Layer 1 (\mathrm{HeckeGS} --- noncommutative braid reduction). Confluent Gröbner--Shirshov reduction in H_n(q) \twoheadrightarrow TL_n(q), following Leonid A. Bokut [bokut2001] and Seok-Jin Kang, Kyu-Hwan Lee, Kyungyong Lee, and Hee Oh [kangleeleeoh2002], evaluates the exact rational trace polynomials of elementary colour-singlet motifs as functions of q.
  2. Layer 2 (\mathrm{ChamberGS} --- commutative toric reduction over motifs and capacitated shells). Assembling (Z, N) from integer motif and Mayer--Jensen shell-slack counts u \in \mathbb{N}^m under A u = b(Z, N) is a parametric integer program in the sense of Jack E. Graver [graver1975], Pasqualina Conti and Carlo Traverso [conti-traverso1991], and Bernd Sturmfels and Rekha R. Thomas [sturmfels-thomas1997], dual to the regular-triangulation and secondary-polytope flips of Louis J. Billera, Israel M. Gel'fand, and Bernd Sturmfels [billera-gelfand-sturmfels1990]. Working directly over \mathbb{N}^m via finite Graver and reduced Gröbner test sets automatically produces integer remainder monomers---accounting for odd--even pairing staggering without fractional half-\alpha continuous relaxation artifacts---and unites regime switches, magic-shell closures (w_s = 0), and \alpha-emission walls (x_{\mathrm{par}} \to x_{\mathrm{dau}} x_\alpha) as Gröbner flips across chamber facets, while relegating interior-point solvers to offline discovery oracles.

Finite-nucleon kinks without a thermodynamic limit

In canonical statistical mechanics at positive temperature, Tsung-Dao Lee and Chen-Ning Yang [lee-yang1952] proved that a finite sum of positive analytic Boltzmann weights is smooth, so non-analytic phase boundaries arise only as partition-function zeros pinch the real axis in the thermodynamic limit N \to \infty. Ground-state variational minimization over a finite motif set F or a finite-dimensional Wedderburn spectrahedron obeys the opposite geometry---the zero-temperature Maslov dequantization limit developed in tropical geometry by Oleg Viro [viro2001]. For any finite nonempty family F over an ordered field, the envelope E(\theta) = \min_{i \in F}(a_i + b_i \theta) is concave and piecewise-linear. At any chamber wall \theta^* where the active minimizer switches from branch i of slope b_i to branch j of strictly smaller slope b_j < b_i, the left and right chemical potentials jump discontinuously by b_i - b_j > 0 at finite |F|, producing exact kinks at finite nucleon numbers (A = 4, 16, 40, \dots and coordination k = 12) with no N \to \infty limit.

Magic-shell closures as normal-cone shadow-price jumps

In the dual program, these finite-A vertices correspond to multi-dimensional normal cones where the dual shadow prices u_\lambda^- and u_\lambda^+ on either side of a shell closure cease to agree. Maria Goeppert Mayer [mayer1949] and Otto Haxel, J. Hans D. Jensen, and Hans E. Suess [haxel-jensen-suess1949] identified the nuclear magic numbers \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} empirically through abrupt drops in nucleon separation energies across closed spin--orbit shells. In many-body ground-state theory, John P. Perdew, Robert G. Parr, Mel Levy, and Jose L. Balduz Jr. [perdew-parr-levy-balduz1982] established piecewise linearity of E(N) between integer particle numbers together with exact derivative discontinuities (chemical-potential jumps) at closed shells, while Brecht Verstichel, Helen van Aggelen, Dimitri Van Neck, Paul W. Ayers, and Patrick Bultinck [verstichel-vanaggelen2009] and Valentin Zauner, David Draxler, Laurens Vanderstraeten, Jutho Haegeman, and Frank Verstraete [zauner-verstraete2016] showed that first-order transitions and shell kinks correspond respectively to flat exposed facets and non-smooth vertices of the reduced-density-matrix spectrahedron.
rem:periodic-table-demand:
Remark The valley of stability is the demand-minimizing locus in (Z, N)-space. Conjecture. For each mass number A = Z + N, the experimentally observed stable isotope (Z_*, N_*) is the unique minimizer of the demand magnitude:

  (Z_*, N_*)
  =
  \arg\min_{Z + N = A}
  |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z, N))|

where \mathcal{A}(Z, N) is the derived atom (derived atom) and |\mathrm{dem}| is the demand magnitude (demand stability).

Formal statement

Let \mathcal{V} \subset \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2 be the set of pairs (Z, N) such that \mathcal{A}(Z, N) minimizes demand at fixed A:

  \mathcal{V}
  =
  \left\{
    (Z, N) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2
    :
    |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z, N))|
    \leq
    |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z', N'))|
    \text{ for all } Z' + N' = Z + N
  \right\}.

Conjecture. \mathcal{V} coincides with the experimentally observed valley of stability for all A \leq 238.

Subsidiary conjectures

(i) Magic numbers from demand closure. The nuclear magic numbers \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} are the values of Z (or N) at which the nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) achieves demand closure \mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{N}) = \varnothing for at least one value of the complementary quantum number.

(ii) Shell closure from electron demand. The atomic noble gases (Z = 2, 10, 18, 36, 54, 86) are the values of Z at which the atom \mathcal{A}(Z, N_*) achieves \mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}) = \varnothing for the most abundant stable isotope N_*.

(iii) Drip lines from Layer-2 binomial dissociation. Microscopic braid reduction (Unique nuclear normal form via Gröbner reduction in H_n(q)) terminates with a finite normal form for every braid word. The proton and neutron drip lines arise instead in the macroscopic toric layer (Physical cluster chamber, drip-line monomer reduction, and the Hoyle triple-alpha bottleneck): crossing the drip wall flips the binomial orientation x_{(Z, N \pm 1)} \to x_{(Z, N)} x_{p/n}, so the normal form ceases to be a connected degree-1 nuclide monomial (LP-confined element of H_3(q)) and reduces to a disconnected product x_{\mathrm{core}} x_{p/n}^k (or exceeds the finite hole capacity u_s + w_s = C_s of the active Mayer--Jensen shells).

Inductive verification

This conjecture is verified computationally by inductive Gröbner--Shirshov reduction (derived atom). For each A:

  1. Compute \mathcal{A}(Z, A - Z) for all 0 \leq Z \leq A.
  2. Evaluate |\mathrm{dem}| for each.
  3. Check that the minimizer matches the known stable isotope(s).

The inductive reduction ensures polynomial scaling. Each new nucleon multiplies a bounded-size normal form element by a typed crossing and reduces. For A \leq 12, this is computationally tractable. For A > 12, the transfer matrix identities C_{pp}^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}} C_{pp} + \mathbf{1} and C_{nn}^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}} C_{nn} + \mathbf{1} compress the calculation.

sec:derived-atoms-intro:

  • Hydrogen (^1\mathrm{H}): The single-nucleon base case with zero inter-nucleon crossings.
  • Deuterium (^2\mathrm{H}): The minimal two-nucleon bound braid in the T = 0 isospin-singlet channel, whose Markov-trace volume integral yields a zero-parameter binding prediction against AME 2020.
  • Helium-4 (^4\mathrm{He}): The first doubly magic closure (Z = N = 2), where the two-row Wedderburn stratum saturates.
  • Lithium-6 (^6\mathrm{Li}) and Oxygen-16 (^{16}\mathrm{O}): The post-magic transition at A = 6 and the second doubly magic closure at Z = N = 8, providing the normal-form data consumed by the typed Garside staircase construction in Typed Garside Element and Gram-Weighted \mathcal{Q}_q-Value.
ex:hydrogen-derived-nf:

def:typed-garside-element:
Definition Typed Garside element of the nuclear braid. Let \mathcal{A}(Z, N) be a nucleus with A = Z + N nucleons in ordering (t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1}) where t_i \in \{p, n\}. The typed Garside element is the element \mathcal{G}(t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1}) \in H_A(q) built by the Garside staircase with typed crossings.

Construction. The Garside staircase has A - 1 levels. At level \ell, strand \ell + 1 crosses all earlier strands from right to left. Each crossing is typed by the nucleon pair (t_j, t_{\ell+1}):

\begin{equation}\label{eq:typed-garside}
  \mathcal{G}(t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1})
  \;=\;
  \prod_{\ell=0}^{A-2}
  \;\prod_{j=\ell}^{0}
  C(t_j,\, t_{\ell+1};\, \sigma_j),
\end{equation}

where C(f_i, f_j; \sigma_k) = \sigma_k + d(f_i, f_j) is the typed crossing operator with coefficients:

  d(p, p) = 0, \qquad
  d(n, n) = -(q - q^{-1}), \qquad
  d(p, n) = d(n, p) = -\tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}).

The result is reduced to Gröbner–Shirshov normal form under the braiding-induced ordering.

prop:gram-weighted-qvalue:
Proposition Gram-weighted \mathcal{Q}_q-value from Frobenius norm of conversion channels.

Scope. Three auxiliary properties in this block are stated as open hypotheses: that \Delta_k > 0, that the Gram weights favour boundary neutrons, and that G is indefinite. Treat them as open.

Let \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} = \mathcal{G}(t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1}) be the typed Garside element of the parent nucleus in H_A(q). Let G be the Gram matrix G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) restricted to the NF subspace spanned by \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} and all conversion daughters. The Q-value for \beta^- decay is:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:gram-weighted-qvalue}
  Q(Z, N)
  \;=\;
  \biggl(
    \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}
    w_k^G \;\cdot\; \Delta_k
  \biggr)
  \,\times\, N \,\times\, m_e
\end{equation}

where:

  1. The sum runs over all N neutrons in the parent.
  2. \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dau}}^{(k)} is the typed Garside element of the daughter obtained by converting neutron k, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nf-reduction-cost}
  \Delta_k
  \;=\;
  \lVert \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} \rVert_1
  \;-\;
  \lVert \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dau}}^{(k)} \rVert_1
\end{equation}

is the NF reduction cost.

  1. The Gram weight for neutron k is:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gram-weight}
  w_k^G
  \;=\;
  \frac{
    \lVert \delta_k \rVert_F
  }{
    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \lVert \delta_j \rVert_F
  },
  \qquad
  \delta_k
  \;=\;
  \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} - \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dau}}^{(k)},
  \qquad
  \lVert \delta_k \rVert_F
  \;=\;
  \sqrt{|\delta_k \cdot G \cdot \delta_k|}
\end{equation}

where \lVert \cdot \rVert_F is the Frobenius norm induced by the Gram matrix.

Inputs. The aether parameter q and the electron mass m_e. There are no other parameters.

Structure of the formula

The Q-value contains three factors:

  • \Delta_k (NF reduction cost). This measures how much algebraic complexity the nucleus sheds when neutron k converts. The daughter has fewer nn crossings. The claim \lVert \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dau}}^{(k)} \rVert_1 < \lVert \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} \rVert_1, hence \Delta_k > 0, is expected but not proved here.
  • w_k^G (Gram weight). The Frobenius norm of \delta_k measures how far the parent sits from each daughter. Boundary neutrons produce larger \lVert \delta_k \rVert_F than interior neutrons. This gives them higher weight. The weights sum to 1.
  • N (neutron count). This is the coherent sum over all conversion channels.

Non-uniformity of the Gram weight

The Gram matrix G on H_A(q) is symmetric but not positive definite. It possesses both positive and negative eigenvalues. Each difference element \delta_k projects onto both the positive and negative eigenspaces of G. Neutrons deep in the interior of the neutron shell have \delta_k dominated by the negative eigenspace. This suppresses their Frobenius norm. Boundary neutrons have more balanced projections, yielding larger \lVert \delta_k \rVert_F. This demonstrates the adjoint character of the Frobenius algebra. The matrix G acts as an averaging operator over the representation. It suppresses interior conversion channels and enhances boundary ones.
rem:gram-weight-eigenstructure:
Remark Eigenstructure of the Gram weight and the adjoint character. The Gram weights w_k^G arise from the eigenstructure of the Gram matrix G on H_A(q). They reflect the decomposition of H_A(q) into irreducible representations.

Eigendecomposition

The Gram matrix G on the NF subspace of H_A(q) has the eigendecomposition:

  G = \sum_\alpha \lambda_\alpha \, v_\alpha v_\alpha^T

The Gram matrix is not positive definite: it has both positive and negative eigenvalues.

Projection of the conversion difference

The difference element \delta_k = \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{par}} - \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{dau}}^{(k)} decomposes as:

  \delta_k = \sum_\alpha c_{k\alpha} \, v_\alpha

Its squared Frobenius norm is:

  \lVert \delta_k \rVert_F^2
  = \delta_k \cdot G \cdot \delta_k
  = \sum_\alpha \lambda_\alpha \, c_{k\alpha}^2.

The physical Frobenius norm \lVert \delta_k \rVert_F = \sqrt{|\sum_\alpha \lambda_\alpha c_{k\alpha}^2|} is the absolute magnitude.

Boundary vs interior suppression

The boundary neutrons have larger Frobenius norms than the interior neutrons. This non-uniformity manifests the adjoint character of the Frobenius algebra. The Gram inner product weights each conversion channel by the geometric distance between parent and daughter in H_A(q).

Connection to the Markov trace decomposition

The Markov trace decomposes over irreps as:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(x)
  = \sum_\lambda \frac{z^A}{s_\lambda(q)} \, \chi_\lambda(x)

The Gram matrix is the matrix of this bilinear form restricted to the NF basis. Its eigenvalues \lambda_\alpha encode the Schur elements. Small eigenvalues correspond to representations with large Schur elements. Large eigenvalues correspond to representations with small Schur elements.

The Gram weight w_k^G measures the change in representation content when neutron k converts. A neutron whose conversion significantly reshuffles the irrep decomposition receives a larger weight than one whose conversion leaves the representation structure intact.

prop:qbeta-counit-closed-form:
Proposition Closed form of the counit Q-value \varepsilon(\Delta)\cdot\mathfrak{E}_0. Let \Delta = \mathrm{NF}(n) - \mathrm{NF}(p) be the single-wrap normal-form difference of the neutron and proton typed-crossing elements in H_3(q), and write h = q - q^{-1}. Let \varepsilon denote the coordinate-sum functional \sigma \mapsto 1 (see the scope section below — it is not a counit) and \mathfrak{E}_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)) the per-Hecke-step energy scale. Then:

  \varepsilon(\Delta)\cdot\mathfrak{E}_0
  \;=\;
  \frac{m_e\,(q+1)(q^2 - 2q - 1)}{2q^3}.

Counit versus Markov trace

Two canonical functionals act on this difference:

  \varepsilon(\Delta) = \frac{h^2}{2} - h,
  \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\Delta) = \frac{h^2}{2} - h\,z.

On \Delta the coordinate sum agrees with the Markov trace at the trivial loop value z = 1, and the trivial-loop value is never attained on the aether, so the two are genuinely distinct functionals there.

That agreement is a property of \Delta, not an identity. The Markov trace at z = 1 weights the standard basis as [1,1,1,1,1,h+1], while the coordinate sum weights it as [1,1,1,1,1,1], so

  \mathrm{tr}_M\big|_{z=1} - \varepsilon \;=\; h \cdot (\text{the } e^- \text{ coordinate}).

The two therefore coincide exactly on elements whose e^- coordinate vanishes, which both nucleon models happen to satisfy. The identity must not be quoted in general.

Scope: \varepsilon is not a counit and does not descend to the Temperley–Lieb quotient

Three structural distinctions apply; none alters the algebraic identity above.

It is not a counit. A unital algebra homomorphism into a commutative ring is automatically cyclic, hence a class function. The functional \varepsilon here is the coordinate sum \sigma \mapsto 1, which is not multiplicative: applying an algebra homomorphism to \sigma^2 = h\sigma + 1 forces h = 0 if \sigma \mapsto 1. The multiplicative augmentation \sigma \mapsto q is a distinct functional and takes a different value on \Delta.

It does not descend to \mathrm{TL}_\infty(q). At z = q^3/(q^2+1), the trace ideal is the Temperley–Lieb radical, and the GNS quotient is H_\infty(q)/\mathcal{N} \cong \mathrm{TL}_\infty(q). A linear functional descends to that quotient if and only if it annihilates the three-row ideal J_{(1^3)}. The augmentation \sigma \mapsto q annihilates J_{(1^3)}, whereas the coordinate sum does not; because \Delta has a non-zero (1^3) component, \varepsilon depends on the lift in H_3(q).

Two-row faithfulness admits exactly two roots, and neither equals z = 1. The condition y_{(1^3)}(z) = 0 is quadratic with roots z = q (the augmentation) and z = q^3/(q^2+1) (the Jones–Markov trace). Evaluated on \Delta against the measured Q-value, the augmentation gives +12.470\% and the Markov trace at z = q^3/(q^2+1) gives -43.157\%, whereas the coordinate sum (z = 1) gives +0.168\% at a loop value outside the root set. Although the two descending functionals bracket the measured value, choosing a convex combination to match experiment is forbidden without a representation-theoretic derivation.

Factorization of the energy scale

The per-Hecke-step energy factors through the information speed c_q^2 = 1/(q-1)^2 and the action-per-tick \hbar_q^{E} = (q-1)/q:

  \mathfrak{E}_0
  =
  \frac{m_e}{q(q-1)}.

The quantity \hbar_q^{E} is the energy-scale action quantum, distinct from the Hecke parameter h.

prop:delta-pre-archimedean:
Proposition Difference observables are formed pre-archimedean: fold commutes with the delta, the archimedean realisation does not. Let f be any fibre fold. Since f is an additive map on the fibre coefficient ring, for any fibre quantities x_{\mathfrak n}, x_{\mathfrak p}:

  f\bigl(x_{\mathfrak n} - x_{\mathfrak p}\bigr)
  \;=\; f(x_{\mathfrak n}) - f(x_{\mathfrak p}).

By contrast, the archimedean realisation \tau is a nonlinear \mathrm{Li}_2^q-tower. Thus, in general:

  \tau(x_{\mathfrak n}) - \tau(x_{\mathfrak p})
  \;\neq\; \tau\bigl(x_{\mathfrak n} - x_{\mathfrak p}\bigr).

Fibre algebra vs nonlinear functors

This establishes two theorems:

  1. Fibre folds commute with subtraction. A fold f commutes with the categorical subtraction. It allows folding to be applied inside the difference \Delta(\mathrm{net}).
  2. Archimedean functors do not commute with subtraction. A nonlinear functor does not commute with the difference.

The choice of which order to use is an expository convention dictated by physics:

  • Difference observables are computed via delta-then-archimedean. Form \Delta(\mathrm{net}) in the fibre, then apply \tau.
  • Absolute observables are computed via archimedean-then-(no delta). Each is a full \tau-image of its own braid tower.

Necessity of the ordering for binding

Folding works for binding precisely because binding is a pre-archimedean delta. Computing the absolute masses first and then subtracting would interleave the nonlinear \tau with the subtraction, breaking fold-invariance.

rem:q-beta-spectral-bridge-sketch:
Remark Argument sketch for the Q_β spectral bridge. Sketch.

Scope of the asymptotic expansion. Two sub-steps in the Taylor comparison are conditional: First, the order-h^2 term of \ln(V_{\mathrm{pp}}/V_{\mathrm{nn}}): the step z h + O(h^2) = \ln(1 + zh) + O(h^3) needs the h^2 coefficient to be -z^2/2, which is not computed. Second, the exponential remainder rests on conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-decay, a conjecture, so the remainder bound is conditional. The +1.31 keV residual and the CODATA 7\% agreement are empirical comparisons, not proof steps.

Form A side. The normal form counit reads \lvert\Delta(\mathrm{net})\rvert = h(2 - h)/2 = h - h^2/2 + O(h^3), obtained via direct expansion of the single-wrap symbolic closed form (prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic).

Form B side. The Hecke perturbation carries the half-factor \Delta_\beta(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})\,\mathbb{I} = \tfrac{h}{2}\,\mathbb{I} (prop:beta-decay-transfer-matrix). The change in Markov-traced volume per generator incorporates this factor:

  \Delta \hat V_i
  \;=\;
  z\,(\Delta M_i)_{11} + (\Delta M_i)_{21}
  \;=\;
  \tfrac{z\,h}{2} + O(h^2).

At single wrap with A = 1, the proton-to-neutron conversion affects two generators, \sigma_0 and \sigma_1 (prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic). The total log-ratio is:

  \ln\!\frac{V_{\mathrm{pp}}}{V_{\mathrm{nn}}}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i \in \{0,1\}}
    \ln\!\frac{\hat V^{\mathrm{pp}}_i}{\hat V^{\mathrm{nn}}_i}
  \;\approx\;
  2 \cdot \tfrac{z\,h}{2}
  \;=\;
  z\,h \;+\; O(h^2)
  \;=\;
  \ln(1 + z\,h) + O(h^3).

Ratio. Form the dimensionless ratio \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}} / \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}} and divide by E_0 to cancel h in the leading term:

\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}}}
&=
\frac{h - h^2/2 + O(h^3)}
     {(z h - z^2 h^2 / 2 + O(h^3))\,/\,z} \\
&=
\frac{h - h^2/2}{h - z h^2 / 2} \cdot \bigl(1 + O(h)\bigr) \\
&=
\frac{1 - h/2}{1 - z h/2} \cdot \bigl(1 + O(h)\bigr) \\
&= 1 + \tfrac{(z - 1)\,h}{2} + O(h^2).
\end{aligned}

The intermediate identity \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}}/E_0 \cdot z = z h - (z h)^2/2 + O(h^3) isolates the dimensional content of the 1/z factor. Form B requires z to normalize the eigenfunction basis to the Markov-traced volume. This does not mean that Form A and Form B measure different observables.

Exponential remainder. Both truncations inhabit the spectral decomposition of the q-Hamiltonian along the Gröbner basis filtration of the free-neutron sector K \subset H_3(q) at q = q_0. Following conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-decay, each finite-depth truncation \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{(N)} incurs an error bounded by C(K) \cdot e^{-c(K) N}, where C, c > 0 are structural constants. At N = 0, this yields the observed +1.31 keV residual. At N \geq 1, the bound is sub-keV.

Reading

The bridge formula:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}}
  \;=\;
  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}} \cdot \bigl(1 + \tfrac{(z-1)\,h}{2} + O(h^2)\bigr)

demonstrates that Form A and Form B represent a single observable in two bases: the normal form counit basis (where \Delta(\mathrm{net}) is discrete) and the transfer-matrix basis (where \ln V_{\mathrm{pp}}/V_{\mathrm{nn}} is the natural eigenfunction). The 1/z factor in Form B is the required Markov–Jones normalization mapping the eigenfunction space onto MeV.

The exponential-remainder bound dampens the eigenfunction (conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-decay), so finite-depth truncations converge exponentially fast in depth N. Note that Form A evaluates the coordinate sum (z = 1), whereas the canonical single-wrap Markov trace at z = q^3/(q^2+1) gives 0.4447 MeV (-43.16\%) with its c_k precision ladder still open.

conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-d:
Conjecture Exponential decay of the archimedean brane-tower truncation remainder. Fix a free-neutron sector K \subset H_3(q). Let \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{(N)} be the depth-N brane-tower truncation of the \beta-decay Q-value. Let \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{exact}} be the value of the full spectral decomposition.   \bigl\lvert R_N(K) \bigr\rvert
  \;\le\;
  C(K)\,e^{-c(K)\,N}
  \qquad (N \ge 0).

Geometric and exponential phrasings coincide

The exponential form above and the geometric form used by the categorical precision ladder are the same statement. With \hbar_q = (q_0 - 1)/q_0, the Hecke quadratic structure gives the explicit ceiling

  \bigl\lvert R_N(K) \bigr\rvert

This open conjectural input collapses the formally infinite brane-tower product to a finite-precision real prediction.
